rules.night: A night is one run_start and the records after it up to the next one; the run resumes each night. Its date is the date it started, on the clock of the card's host.
rules.classes: Coverage is evidence about the thing that ran. A slice swept on one RTL tree says nothing about another, so a tile item is counted per RTL tree, and a host item per host tree and compiler, because no tile computes it. A changed tree starts a new class from nothing, and nothing is summed across classes. How a run that did not record its tree is placed is the report's rule, and the class's label says which.
rules.groups: Within a class the items are in two groups, each counted over its own items and spaces so that a group joining a class does not move the other's figures: the base items, and the wide-format items (fp64, fp128 and fp256), which exist only in a tool built against the pinned MPFR. A class's total is over both. Each item names the format it computes in; a conversion names both ends.
rules.estimate: ESTIMATE, not a measurement. For an item not yet fully covered in a current class: its gain over the class's last 3 nights (fewer if the class is younger), divided by the nights in that window, is its rate a night; the nights left are the remaining indices over that rate, rounded up; the date counts that many days after the newest night, assuming a night every day. It does not know of a skipped night, or that items finishing free time for the rest.
rules.card_time: Time on the card is the report's: the union of the battery and sweep legs' intervals on the card images, skipped legs and the host pool's legs left out. The wall span runs from the first record to the last and includes the days between nights.
